argv: Completed M1 with one accepted provider-neutral contract authority, explicit capability discovery and failure semantics, deterministic compatibility fixtures and generated Rust bindings, a strict standalone conformance provider, and checked-in drift enforcement.

Evidence: product/contracts/memory-provider-v1/contract-set.json is the single ordered authority for the accepted registry, handshake, observation, recall, lifecycle, and terminal contracts, each with a strict versioned schema and focused validator. The registry exposes three mandatory and twelve optional behavior capabilities without provider-name branching; unsupported required capabilities and lifecycle operations return explicit typed outcomes, while unknown optional extensions round-trip as opaque inert payloads. Twenty-five canonical JSONL goldens cover success, zero results, degradation, cancellation, timeout, incompatibility, stale scope, malformed input, unknown optional and required extensions, idempotent duplicates, conflicts, partial effects, and unknown effects. Deterministic generated Rust bindings carry source/generator/output digests and compile without transport or provider coupling. The isolated Rust 2024 dummy provider passes twenty-three mandatory, idempotency, exact-scope, cancellation/deadline, snapshot/restart, extension, and unsupported-operation journeys under forbid(unsafe_code), deny(warnings/missing_docs), and strict Clippy. The product-memory-contracts workflow mirrors its product-owned authority and checks every contract, mutation suite, golden, generated binding, dummy provider, patch policy, and clean checkout on push and pull request.
